activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
fact: When a grown-up cuts an onion, it can make their eyes sting and water.
story:
Elias wants to make soup for his family. He and Dad go to the big community kitchen. There is a long table and many pots.

Elias picks a carrot and a potato. He puts them in the pot. Then he picks a big white onion. "This one," he whispers, like a little mouse.

Dad cuts the onion with his knife. Elias stands back, where it is safe. Then Dad rubs his eyes. Water runs down his face.

Elias feels worried. "Dad, are you sad?" he asks. "Did the soup make you cry?"

Dad laughs a soft laugh. "No, no," he says. "It is just the onion. Onions can make eyes water."

Elias looks at the onion. He looks at Dad's wet eyes. He blinks his own eyes. They feel fine. Dad did not cut an onion near him.

The soup bubbles. A grown-up stirs the hot pot. Soon the soup is ready. Mom and baby sister come to the table. They eat the warm soup. It is yummy.

Baby sister makes a funny face. Dad smiles at her. His eyes are all dry now.

Elias holds up the onion. "This made you cry," he says.

"I will cut it far away next time," says Dad.

Elias giggles and spoons more soup into his bowl.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
fact: We smell with our nose.
story:
Sara sat at the kitchen table. Grandma put a bowl of soup in front of her. The soup was too hot, so Grandma blew on it. Sara would wait.

While she waited, Sara played a game. "My eyes see," she said. She looked at the steam. It went up high. "My ears hear." She listened to the pot on the stove. Bub, bub, bub.

Then Grandma said, "Sniff, sniff." Sara sniffed with her nose. The soup smelled like carrots. "Mmm," said Sara. "I smell with my nose!" She touched the warm bowl with one finger. It was still hot, so she pulled her hand back.

At last the soup was ready. Sara took a small sip. It tasted yummy. "Grandma," she said, "my tongue tastes it!" Grandma laughed. Outside, a dog began to bark. Sara pointed at the window. "My ears hear that too!" she said.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
fact: Opposites are two words that mean things as different as they can be, like big and small.
story:
Isla went to the playground with her towel. She wanted to play the opposite game with her friend Tom. Tom said a word. Then Isla had to shout the opposite. Tom said, "Big!" Isla looked at the big slide. She shouted, "Small!" and pointed at the small slide. "Yes!" said Tom. He laughed and clapped.

They ran to the swings. Tom said, "Fast!" Isla pumped her legs. Her swing went fast. Then she let it slow down. "Slow!" she shouted. Tom said, "You got it!" Next Tom said, "Hot!" He pointed at the sun on the bench. Isla touched the cold metal bar of the swing. "Cold!" she shouted. "Right again," said Tom.

Then Tom said, "Awake!" Isla stood very still. She thought hard. She closed one eye. Then she opened both eyes wide. "Asleep!" she shouted. Tom fell over laughing. "That was the best one," he said. Isla bowed on her swing. "Let's play more tomorrow," she said. Tom nodded and grinned.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
fact: A rectangle has four sides and four square corners, like the shape of a door.
story:
Samuel's class went on a shape hunt. Miss Patel said, "Find me a circle!" Samuel found a round clock on the wall. "Find me a square!" He found a square block, red and smooth.

Then Miss Patel said, "Find a rectangle." Samuel frowned. What did a rectangle look like? He looked and looked. Then his friend Lily pointed at the door. "That's one!" Samuel ran to the door. He touched the top side. He touched the bottom side. He touched the two long sides. Four sides! Then he pressed his finger in each corner. One, two, three, four. Square corners, just like his block. The door was a rectangle!

Samuel was so quiet while he counted that Lily started to giggle. "You look like a sleepy cat by that door!" she said. Samuel heard a coat zip open behind him. Tom pulled off his coat and laid it flat on the rug. "Look, my coat is a rectangle too!" Everyone laughed and clapped. Then Miss Patel opened the door. "Snack time," she said, and twelve happy kids ran through the big rectangle at once.

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: Taking turns means each person gets a go, one after another.
story:
Olivia wanted to paint at the little table. Her brother Sam wanted to paint too. But there was only one big brush left.

"Who gets the brush?" Olivia asked herself. "We both get a go," she said. "One after another."

So Olivia went first. She painted a cloudy sky on her paper. Sam watched and waited. Then she put the brush down. "Your turn, Sam," she said.

Sam went next. He painted a red wall with a door in it. Olivia watched and waited. Then it was her turn again.

Outside, the rain stopped. Sam looked at the window. "Can we play now?" he asked.

"Yes," said Olivia. She helped Sam fix the paint lid. It was tight, so she pushed with two hands. Click!

They ran to the door. "You first," said Sam. "No, you first," said Olivia. They both laughed and went out together.

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
fact: A new baby must be touched very gently.
story:
Logan ran into the baby store. His shoes went tap, tap on the floor. "A new baby is coming!" he said. Mom held his hand. "We need tiny things," she said.

They found a cozy blanket. They found a little sock. Then Logan saw a big doll in a basket. The doll looked like a real baby. Mom said, "You can practice."

Logan patted the doll. Pat! Pat! The doll's head tipped over. Mom sat down next to him. "Watch me," she said. She touched the doll's hand with one finger. She moved it slow and soft.

Logan tried. He touched the doll's hand with one finger. Soft. Slower. The doll stayed still. "I did it!" said Logan. "Gentle hands!"

Then the doll made a sound. "Waa," it went. Logan jumped. "The doll talks!"

"The baby will talk too," said Mom. Logan touched the doll's cheek with his soft finger. "I will touch you like this," he whispered. "Nice and slow."

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
fact: People often write their name on their artwork so everyone knows who made it.
story:
Mila sat at the big art table. She drew a big yellow apple. Ben sat next to her. He drew a big yellow apple too.

Miss Rosa said, "Time to put the paintings on the wall." Mila put her painting down. Ben put his down too. The two paintings touched on the table.

Then Mila looked. She saw two yellow apples. She could not tell which one was hers. "Which apple did I paint?" she asked.

Miss Rosa said, "Let's look very closely." Ben pointed at his paper. His paper had letters on it. The letters said BEN. "That one is mine," he said. "My mom helped me write my name."

Mila looked at her paper. It had no name on it. It was just a yellow apple. "Mine is this one," she said softly. "It has no name."

After that, Mila got a small pencil. She wrote M-I-L-A at the top. She sent her painting to the wall with the tape. Her name rode on top of the apple, all the way up.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: In baseball, the batter wears a helmet to protect their head.
story:
Ellie ran to the plate to bat. She was so excited to hit the ball. "Wait, Ellie!" said Coach Ben. "Come back here first."

Ellie ran back. Coach Ben held up a white helmet. "Put this on," he said. Ellie put the helmet on her head. It felt big and warm.

Then Ellie batted. The ball flew far! Everyone clapped. "We might win!" said her friend Sam. Ellie smiled under her helmet. She patted it with her little hand. "My helmet," she said. Coach Ben gave her a thumbs up. Ellie ran to first base, and the helmet stayed snug on her head the whole way.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: When you play house, each person can pick a role, like the parent or the baby.
story:
Brooks ran to the playground. He wanted to play house. His friend Mia was there by the little play kitchen. "Let's play house," said Brooks. "I want to be the parent," said Mia. "I want to be the parent too," said Brooks. They both stood still. They both frowned.

Then Mia had an idea. "You be the parent first," she said. "Then we switch. I will be the baby now." Brooks liked that. He picked up the pot and stirred it. The pot went clink, clink, clink. Mia lay down near the little bed. "Time to sleep, baby," said Brooks. He patted her head. One pat, two pats, three pats.

"Now we switch," said Brooks. Mia jumped up. She was the parent now. Brooks was the baby. He crawled to the toy bear and hugged it tight. Mia covered the bear with a small blanket. "The baby bear is cold," she said. Brooks rocked the bear back and forth. The bear went rock, rock, rock.

They played until the sun went low. "Same time tomorrow?" asked Mia. "Yes," said Brooks. He thought about tomorrow all the way home. "I can be the baby again," he said to his mom. "Or the parent."

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
fact: Taking one object away from a group makes the number one smaller.
story:
Clara went to the community centre with her dad. There was a big table with crayons. Clara sat down on a small chair.

Her friend Mia sat down too. Miss Anne gave them each a tray. Clara counted her crayons. "One, two, three, four, five," she said. "I have five crayons." Mia counted hers. "One, two, three, four," said Mia. Clara had more. Clara smiled.

Clara drew a tall tree and a little car. Then the bell on the wall began to ring. Snack time! Miss Anne gave each girl one strawberry. Clara ate her strawberry. It was sweet and red.

Then Clara looked at her tray. One crayon was gone. It had rolled under the table. Clara picked it up and put it back. Then she counted again. "One, two, three, four," she said. "One crayon less, one number less." She took it away once more and counted. "One, two, three."

Mia slid her tray next to Clara's. "Now we both have four," said Clara. Mia laughed. The girls lined up all eight crayons in a tall, tall tower, and Clara counted every one.

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
fact: After brushing, you spit the toothpaste out instead of swallowing it.
story:
Lena sat in a big blue chair. The waiting room had a fish tank. A little orange fish swam past her nose. Lena was awake early today. Today she would see the dentist for the first time.

A nurse called her name. Lena held Mama's hand. The dentist showed Lena a small cup of water. Then Lena brushed her teeth with minty paste. Her mouth got full of white foam. It tasted like mint. Lena closed her mouth to swallow it.

Then she stopped. She leaned over the sink. She pushed the foam out with her tongue. "Good job," said the dentist. "You spit it out." Lena picked a green card with a star on it. The nurse gave her a sticker too. On the way home, Lena smiled at the orange fish in her mind.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
fact: Swim teachers often have children practice blowing bubbles into the water through their mouth.
story:
Raphael stood by the lake pool. The water looked cool and shiny. His teacher, Mia, smiled at him.

"Put your face near the water," said Mia.

Raphael shook his head. "Will it tickle my nose?" he asked.

"Try it and see," said Mia.

Raphael leaned down. He took a big breath. Then he blew out through his mouth. Glub, glub, glub! Big bubbles popped up all around his chin.

Raphael lifted his head. "Bubbles!" he laughed. "My mouth made them!"

He blew again. More bubbles came. They grew big, then they went pop.

"Look, Mia! More bubbles!"

After the pool, Dad helped Raphael tie the strings on his shoes. Raphael looked at the lake. "Dad, can I blow bubbles in the lake too?"

"Not yet," said Dad. "First you blow them here, at the pool."

Raphael grinned and blew one more big bubble.

activity: getting through an evening power cut at home
knowledge_domain: getting through an evening power cut at home
fact: Books, puzzles and board games can be played without electricity.
story:
The lights went out. Matthew stood in the backyard with his dad. The house was dark. The TV would not turn on.

"How will we watch the bus show?" Matthew asked.

Dad clicked a flashlight on. A bright circle popped onto the grass. "No TV tonight," Dad said. "What else can we do?"

Matthew looked at the dark house. Could a puzzle work with no lights? Dad shined the flashlight on the porch table. Mom brought out a game with a big red box.

"Does a game need light from the wall?" Matthew asked.

"Let's find out," said Mom.

They opened the box. The flashlight lit up the board. Matthew picked a new card. He moved his little dog. It was his turn, then Dad's turn, then Mom's turn. The game worked and worked.

Mom clapped. "No plugs anywhere," she said.

Matthew laughed. He shined the flashlight on his dog piece himself. "You don't need the wall," he told it. The moon stayed up above them, big and white, watching the game.

activity: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
knowledge_domain: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
fact: Soft butter spreads more easily than hard butter straight from the fridge.
story:
Aubrey woke up hungry. She wanted toast with butter. She wanted to butter it all by herself.

Daddy made the toast. The toast was warm and golden. He gave Aubrey the butter and a dull knife. Aubrey pushed the butter on the toast. The butter was cold and hard. It tore a hole in the toast. "Oh no," said Aubrey. "My toast has a hole."

Then Aubrey saw the butter dish on the counter. That butter had sat out all night. It was soft. She tried again. The soft butter slid right across the toast. No holes! "Look, Daddy, it's smooth," she said.

Next came the milk. Aubrey held the cup with one foot planted steady on the floor. She poured slowly. Not one drop spilled. The dog barked, happy for breakfast too. "He wants some," said Aubrey. Daddy filled the dog's bowl.

Aubrey bit into her toast. It was yummy and not stinky at all, like her brother's socks. She laughed. "More toast, please," she said, holding up her cup.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: A book's title is its name.
story:
It was story morning at daycare. Zoey wanted the cat book. The one with the sweet little cat on the cover.

She ran to the bookshelf. So many books! She pointed. "That one? That one? That one?" Her teacher shook her head.

Zoey patted the covers. She turned one book over. The pages flapped. Upside down!

Then she saw it. Big letters on the front. She knew those letters. "Z... O... E... Y?" she asked.

Her teacher laughed. "That says Little Cat." Zoey looked at the big words. "Little Cat," she said slowly. "Little Cat is the book's name!"

"Can I have Little Cat, please?" she asked. "Yes!" said her teacher.

Zoey sat down. She opened the front cover. Page one, page two, page three. The sweet little cat said, "Meow."

"Little Cat," said Zoey. "That is your name."

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
fact: A bright light above the dentist's chair helps the dentist see inside your mouth.
story:
Eliana sat in her car seat. She held her small toy cat. "Today we see the dentist," said Mama. "Will he like my teeth?" Eliana asked. "I think so," said Mama. The car stopped. They went inside.

The dentist had a big chair. It went up and up. Eliana climbed in with help. Then a bright light came on over her head. Eliana squinted. "Too bright," she said. The light made her eyes feel funny.

The dentist smiled. He gave her tiny sunglasses. "Try these," he said. Eliana put them on. Now the light did not hurt her eyes. She opened her mouth wide. The dentist looked inside. "I can see all your teeth," he said. The bright light helped him see.

"Open big like a lion," said the dentist. Eliana opened very big. "I see clean teeth," he said. "You taste your food with those teeth, don't you?" Eliana giggled. After, Mama gave her a sticker. Eliana put it on her toy cat. "Now kitty has sunglasses too," she said.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
fact: Many libraries ask people to use quiet voices so others can read.
story:
Edouard stood in his bedroom. Today he would get his first library card. He put on his blue sweater. "I am ready," he told Mama.

At the library, a kind lady gave him a small card. It had his name on it. Edouard ran to the shelves. He found a big book about dinosaurs. "A DINOSAUR BOOK!" he shouted. Then he saw a girl reading at a table. He saw a man reading by the window. Edouard looked at their quiet faces. He made his voice very small. "A dinosaur book," he whispered. Mama smiled and nodded. The lady stamped his book. Edouard held it tight with both hands.

Back home, Edouard sat on his bed. He opened the dinosaur book. He picked up his crayons. He began to draw a big green dinosaur in his own garden picture. "This is the best day," he whispered.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: A classroom has rules that everyone in the class follows.
story:
Eliana stood at the gate of the school playground. It was her very first day. She wanted to play on the big red slide. But a long line of kids stood there first. Eliana's tummy felt jumpy like a stormy sky.

She looked around. Then she ran to the front of the line. "My turn!" she said. But a boy named Sam shook his head. "No cutting," he said. "We all follow the rules. Miss May told us." Miss May blew her whistle. "Sam is right," she said. "Line up, please."

So Eliana went to the back of the line. She waited. She counted one shoe, two shoes, three shoes. Soon it was her turn. The slide was fast and bumpy. "Whee!" she yelled. Sam slid down next to her. "Your turn again?" he asked. Eliana grinned and said, "Yes, after you!"

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
fact: You open your mouth wide so the dentist can see every tooth.
story:
Brooks sat in his cozy car seat. A big blue plane flew over the car. "The dentist is far away," said Mama. Brooks was going to the dentist for the very first time.

At the dentist, a kind lady asked Brooks to open his mouth. Brooks opened it a little bit. Then he closed it to say, "Is this right?" The lady could not see his teeth. "Try again," she said with a smile.

Brooks took a big breath. He opened his mouth wide, like a lion's roar. Now the lady could see every tooth. She counted them one by one. Brooks jumped down from the big chair. "I did it!" he said. Mama gave him a soft hug. He got a little sticker shaped like a tooth.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
fact: Feelings can show on your face, like a big smile when you are happy.
story:
Lillian wanted to find her happy face. Where could it be? She looked in the hall mirror. First she made a big smile. "There it is!" she said. The mirror girl smiled too.

Then Lillian made a sad face. Her mouth went down, down, down. The mirror girl looked sad too. Lillian made an angry face, all scrunchy. Then a scared face, with wide eyes. Then an excited face, jumping up and down. The mirror jumped with her.

Papa came to see. "Look, Papa!" said Lillian. She showed him every face. Papa tried one too. But his face looked funny, not sad and not mad. Lillian laughed. It was a surprise face! "What is that one?" she asked. Papa laughed too, and the mirror held two laughing faces.

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: When someone is talking, we listen and wait until they finish.
story:
Parker ran into the playroom. He had big news. "A dragon!" he shouted. "At the park!"

Mia was talking first. She was telling about her teddy bear. Parker talked over her. "Dragon, dragon!" he said. Then Mia stopped talking. She folded her arms. Parker had missed the end of the teddy story. Now Mia looked sad, and nobody was talking at all.

Parker sat on the rug. He put his hands in his lap. He watched Mia's mouth and waited. Mia told the end. The teddy hid in a dark cave and found a flashlight. "The end," said Mia. Then she smiled at Parker. "Your turn now," she said. Parker took a big breath. "A green dragon flew over the park!" he said. "It waved at me!" Mia clapped her hands. "Again, again!" she said.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
fact: On your birthday, you turn one year older.
story:
Sophia was three years old. Today she went to the bowling alley for her birthday. "Happy birthday, Sophia!" said Grandma. There were balloons and cake and a big shiny spoon for the ice cream.

Sophia pushed her ball down the lane. The ball rolled and rolled. It hit the pins. All the pins fell down! "Strike!" everyone cheered. The ball made the pins fall. Sophia jumped up and down. She rolled the ball again. The pins fell again.

Then Daddy brought out the cake. He lit the candles with a match, all by himself. Sophia counted the candles. "One, two, three, four," she said. "Four candles? I am three!"

"You had a birthday today," said Mommy. "Now you are one year older."

Sophia looked at the candles. Four candles for four years. She smiled a real big smile. "I am four!" she shouted.

"Make a wish," said Grandma. "But don't forget to blow." Sophia blew out the candles. Out they went, one by one.

"Happy birthday to me," sang Sophia. "I am four, I am four, I am four!" Then she picked up her spoon and took a big bite of cake.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
fact: Mixing blue paint and yellow paint makes green paint.
story:
Parker was at school. It was paint time. He wanted to paint green grass.

Mia wanted green grass too. They looked for the green paint. The green pot was empty. "Oh no," said Mia. "No more green."

Parker had a plan. He got the blue pot. He got the yellow pot. He put blue on his brush. He put yellow on top. He mixed them on the paper. "Look!" said Parker. The paint turned green. Green grass!

Mia smiled. "Let me try." She mixed blue and yellow too. Her grass was green. Parker kept painting. He painted green grass, and a yellow sun, and a blue slide.

At play time, Mia went down the big slide. Parker slid down too. Then he ran back up the old wooden steps. "Again!" he said.

Teacher Kim hung the paintings up to dry. "Beautiful grass," she said. Parker looked at his green grass. "I made green," he told Mia. Mia laughed. "Mix it again tomorrow!"

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
fact: A triangle has three sides and three corners.
story:
Hailey wanted to feed her pet rabbit, Clover. But first Mom called her for lunch. Mom cut the sandwich with a safe knife. The pieces were triangles.

"A triangle," Hailey said. She touched one corner. "One." She touched another. "Two." She touched the last one. "Three."

"Three corners," she said. "Three sides, too." She counted the sides. One, two, three. Then she took a big bite.

After lunch, Hailey made shapes for Clover. She folded a paper square. She cut out a circle. She pulled a napkin into a rectangle. "Which one is like my sandwich?" she asked. She held up the triangle. "This one! It has three corners."

Clover hopped over and sniffed the triangle. Hailey laughed. "You like triangles too," she said. "Here, Clover. One corner for you."

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: A referee or umpire is the person who makes sure players follow the rules.
story:
Natalie put on her red team shirt. She ran into the backyard for soccer. Coach Maria was there. So was a man in a striped shirt. He held a little whistle.

Natalie kicked the ball. Then Ben kicked it. He used his hands to knock it into the net. The man blew his whistle. "No hands," he said.

Natalie frowned. She sat down on the crunchy grass. A soft feather floated by her shoe.

"Why did he stop the game?" Natalie asked.

"His job is to watch the rules," said Coach Maria. "He helps us play fair."

Natalie stood up. She kicked the ball again. This time she used only her foot. The whistle stayed quiet. The man gave her a big thumbs up.

Natalie laughed and kicked the ball to Ben.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: Counting backward from ten down to one is called a countdown.
story:
Isla wanted to be the rocket ship today. But Tom said, "You have to count first." Isla did not know how.

At circle time, Miss Jo sang a counting song. "One, two, three, four, five." Isla sang too. She counted the beads on the table. She counted six, seven, eight. She counted nine crayons, then one more. "Ten!" she said.

Outside, Tom made a rocket from a big box. "Pretend we are going far away," he said. "Past the cow in the field!" Isla climbed in. "Count down," said Tom. "From ten."

Isla took a big breath. "Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. Blast off!" She jumped up so high. "I did it!" said Isla. "Next time I count to the moon."

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
fact: Wet and dry are opposites.
story:
Mila wanted to play with her big teddy bear. But she could not find him. She looked under the small chair. She looked in the slow toy train. No teddy.

Then Mila found a puddle on the floor. The water was cold on her toes. Her socks were wet. "Where did the water come from?" she asked. Mama came in. "The big dog splashed his water bowl," said Mama. "He wagged his tail and tipped it over."

Mila laughed. She took off her wet socks. She put on dry socks, fast. Then she found teddy behind the big basket. She hugged him. "Wet socks off, dry socks on," she said. She said it again, "Wet socks off, dry socks on." Then she rolled the slow train, early for teddy's tea party, all the way to the small chair.

activity: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
knowledge_domain: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
fact: Dirty clothes go in the laundry basket so they can be washed.
story:
Levi loved his blue socks. He wore them at school all day. He ran in them. He jumped in them. He painted in them. Now his socks had red and green paint spots. They felt sticky too.

At nap time, Levi pulled off his socks. He dropped them on the floor. Then he saw something. His friend Milo tossed his socks into a basket. Swish! They landed inside. "That looks fun," said Levi. He picked up his sticky socks. He lifted them high. He aimed at the basket. He threw. The socks hit the edge and fell out.

Levi laughed. He tried again. This time the socks went in. Swish! The basket held Milo's socks too. After school, Teacher Amy carried the basket to the washer. Levi gave the basket a gentle hug. "Bye bye, socks," he said. "Come back clean!" Teacher Amy smiled. "They will," she said.

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: Being fair means everyone gets a chance.
story:
Jack ran to the sand pit at the park. He wanted to build a big castle. There was one box of round buckets and shovels.

Jack took all the buckets. He took all the shovels too. His friend Mia had nothing to hold. Mia sat down and put her hands in her lap. She watched the sand with sad eyes.

Jack looked at Mia. Then he looked at his tall pile. One friend had all the toys. One friend had none. That did not feel right.

Jack gave Mia a red bucket. He gave her a blue shovel too. Mia smiled and began to dig. Soon she had a tall tower. Jack had a tall tower too. Side by side, the towers stood like a gate.

Then Tom came to play. He had nothing at all. Jack thought fast. He held out a green shovel. "You can dig with me," Jack said. Tom dug a deep, cool hole. He made a round moat around both towers.

Three friends played in the sand. Everyone got a chance. The castle grew bigger and bigger. At the end, Jack clapped sand off his hands. "Best castle ever," said Mia.

"Same time tomorrow?" asked Tom. Jack nodded and grinned.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
fact: Hitting a drum harder makes a louder sound.
story:
Beau sat on the small stage in the school auditorium. A big drum sat in front of him. His teacher, Miss Ada, gave him two soft drumsticks. "You can play," she said.

Beu hit the drum very hard. BOOM! The sound was huge. A baby in the back row woke up and began to cry. Beau looked at the baby. He felt his face get warm.

He tried again, this time with a little tap. Tap. The sound was small and soft. The baby blinked and stopped crying. Beau tapped again, soft as a whisper. Tap, tap. Miss Ada smiled. "That sound is just right," she said.

Beau played a slow song with his soft taps. The baby fell back to sleep. Beau looked at his drumsticks and whispered, "Soft taps make soft sounds. That's true." Then he tapped the drum one more time, very gently, and listened.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
fact: Wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
story:
Declan sat in his car seat. He looked out the window. "I see the park!" he said. Mama parked the car. Declan's bike was in the back. His helmet was in the back too.

Declan jumped down. He ran to his bike. He held the handle bars. He wanted to ride right away. Then he saw his helmet sitting in the car. He went back and got it. Mama helped him clip it on. It sat snug on his head.

Declan pushed the pedal. The bike went fast. Then his foot did slip off the pedal. He wobbled and fell down. But the helmet was on his head. His knee got a little bump. It was okay. "Good try," said Mama. "You got your helmet first." Declan got up. The air felt fresh on his face. He pedaled again. This time he rode all the way to the big tree.

"Look at me, Mama!" he called. "I did it!"

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: In basketball, a team scores by getting the ball through the hoop.
story:
Arlo stood in the backyard with his big red ball. Today he had his first game. The ball had to go up and through the hoop. That was how his team got a point.

Arlo threw the ball. It hit the hoop and fell down. He threw it again. It hit the edge and bounced away. "Why won't it go in?" he asked. Maybe the ball was too low? He tried one more time. Too low again. The ball rolled to the grass.

Arlo picked up the ball and looked at the hoop. It was way up high. What if he threw it way up high too? He bent his knees. He pushed the ball up, up, up. The ball sailed through the hoop and dropped down. It went in! It went in! Arlo clapped his hands.

Dad came out with a juicy apple slice. "Big throw!" he said. "You got the ball through the hoop. That's a point for your team." Arlo took a bite and chewed. Then he lined up his ball again. "Watch me," he said. He bent his knees and pushed.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: In pretend play, a cardboard box can become a car, a boat or a house.
story:
Levi found a big cardboard box in the living room. He climbed inside it. Then his friend Mia came over. She wanted the box too.

"I want it to be a boat," said Mia.

"But it is my car," said Levi.

They both held the box. It wobbled. Nobody could play.

Then Levi had an idea. He asked, "Can we take turns?"

"Yes!" said Mia. "First the car."

Levi sat in the box. "Beep beep!" he said. Mia pushed the box a little. The box slid on the floor. Zoom!

Then it was Mia's turn. "Row, row," she said. Levi made waves with his arms. The boat rocked side to side.

Next Levi remembered his teddy bear. Teddy needed a home. So the box became a house. Levi put teddy inside. Mia added a block for a table. She gave teddy a pretend crunchy cracker.

"Teddy is happy," said Levi.

Then Mama called, "Snack time!" Levi and Mia ran to the table. The box sat still, waiting. After snack, the box could be anything again.

"Next it will be a train," said Mia.

Levi smiled. "Choo choo!"

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
fact: A veterinarian, or vet, is a doctor for animals.
story:
Jack had big news. He had a new puppy! The puppy was small and white. Jack named him Socks.

The next morning, Socks did not eat. He just sat there. "Is Socks sick?" Jack asked. Mom felt his nose. "He feels warm," she said. "We need a doctor."

Jack was worried. Socks could not talk to a people doctor! They walked to a special building. Jack opened the door and his eyes got big. A cat sat in a box. A rabbit sat in a lap. A bird dropped one white feather on the floor. "Mom! This doctor has pets everywhere!"

A kind lady in a green coat came out. "I am the vet," she said. "I am a doctor for animals." She looked at Socks. She felt his tummy. She gave him a little drink. "He has a small cold," she said. "He will be fine."

At home, Jack fed Socks his food. Socks gobbled it all up. He wagged his tail and begged for more. Jack laughed and clapped his hands. "Good boy, Socks!" he said.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
fact: In soccer, a team scores a goal by getting the ball into the other team's net.
story:
Elijah sat on the bench with Dad. The ice rink was cold and loud. His breath made little clouds. On the big TV screen, a soccer game was on. Mom gave him fresh popcorn from the machine. His friend Mia sat close by.

A player ran up to the net. "He has to kick it over!" Elijah said. He watched and waited. The ball went low. It rolled on the grass. Elijah held his popcorn tight.

The ball went right into the net. The net moved and swayed. The crowd on TV went wild. Mia clapped her mittens together. The horn at the rink beeped too, for the ice skaters.

"Again, again!" Elijah said. He wanted to see one more. They waited a long time. He ate popcorn, one piece at a time. Then another player ran fast. He kicked the ball low again. The net caught it, soft like a kiss on a blanket. Elijah jumped up so fast he almost dropped his popcorn. Dad caught the bag just in time.

"Right in the net," Elijah whispered. He kept his eye on the screen.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: A pair means two, like a pair of socks.
story:
Isaac sat at the dinner table. He had two feet. But he had one sock on. The other sock was missing. "I want my sock," said Isaac.

Mama said, "Look under your chair." Isaac looked. There it was. One little sock. "A sock needs its partner," said Mama. Isaac held up both socks. "One sock and one sock," he said. "A pair!" Mama nodded. "A pair means two."

Isaac counted his toes as Mama put the socks in the wash. "One, two, three, four, five," he said. Then the other foot. "Six, seven, eight, nine, ten." Ten toes, all warm.

The wash machine made a swishy noise. Isaac listened. Then it was time to eat. Papa set down the plates. "One for Mama, two for Papa, three for Isaac," said Papa. Isaac picked up his spoon. He tapped it once, then twice. "Early dinner tonight," said Mama. Isaac grinned and took a big bite of noodles. "Ten more bites," he said.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: Some languages, like Arabic and Hebrew, are read from right to left.
story:
Margot wanted a story before bed. She picked her big cat book. She opened it. She opened it at the back. "That is the end," said Mama. "Books start at the front." Margot flipped to the front. The words sat in rows, like little ants.

At daycare, her friend Sam had a new book. It opened the other way. "It goes this way," said Sam. He slid his finger from right to left. "That is Hebrew," he said. Margot peeked. The words marched a different way. "Silly words," she said. "They walk the wrong way!" Sam laughed. "Not wrong. Just their way."

At home, Margot found her crayon. She drew one cat, two cats, three stinky cats. She made letters under them. "I will read it to you," she said. She opened her book from the right. She tapped each mark. The cat on the bed began to sink down, sleepy. "Once," read Margot, "there was one stinky cat."

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: Practice is when a team learns skills and gets ready for games.
story:
Noah had a red ball and a little toy horse on the grass. Today his team would come to practice in the backyard. Noah did not want to practice. "I want to play with my horse," he said. His dad smiled. "You can guess what we do at practice," Dad said. "I guess we throw the ball," said Noah.

The team came. They threw the ball to each other. Noah dropped it the first time. He dropped it the second time too. Then he threw it again and again. His hands learned to close at the right time. At last he caught the ball. "I got it!" he said.

On Saturday the team had a game. The sun was warm. A boy on the other team threw the ball far. Noah ran. He put out his hands. He caught it, just like at practice. Everyone clapped. "You were not late today," said Dad. Noah held the ball up high. "Practice made my hands ready," he said, and he ran to play again.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
fact: Feelings change, so a sad feeling can turn into a happy one later.
story:
Gabriel woke up excited. Today was park day. He put on his red shoes all by himself. "Park! Park!" he sang.

Then he heard rain. Tap, tap, tap on the window. Gabriel looked out. Big drops fell down. No park today. His face felt sad. His eyes got wet too. "The rain took my park," he said.

Mama gave him a hug. "We can still play," she said. "Let's build a fort." Gabriel was angry at the rain at first. He stomped his foot. Then Mama pulled the big blanket off the bed. Gabriel grabbed his soft chair. They made a fort together.

"Come in, come in!" said Gabriel. Inside, he had his teddy bear and a little flashlight. The flashlight was too bright and scared him for a second. He covered it with his hand. Then it was a soft glow. "Cozy," said Gabriel. Mama laughed, and he laughed too.

The rain still tapped outside. But now Gabriel was happy. His sad feeling had gone away. "Fort day is good too," he said. He hugged teddy tight and crawled in deeper.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
fact: Later means some time after now, not right away.
story:
Theodore went to the store with Mama. He saw a big red ball in the middle of the shelf. He wanted it so much. "Can we get the ball now?" he asked.

"Not now," said Mama. "We can get it later. First we need bread and milk."

Theodore held Mama's hand. They found the bread. They found the milk. "Is it later yet?" he asked. "Not yet," said Mama. They walked past the dark coffee corner. Theodore did not kick his feet. He waited.

At last Mama said, "Now it is later. Let's go get your ball." She reached up and took the red ball down. Theodore hugged it tight.

"Today you got a ball," said Mama. "Yesterday we got apples. Tomorrow we can play with the ball at home."

"The ball is mine today!" said Theodore, and he smiled all the way to the car.
